source_basis.source_scope: received WEB Mark coordinate/text surface plus its direct internal canonical cross-reference metadata only
source_basis.editorial_metadata_guard: Headings, paragraphs, punctuation, red letters, footnotes, Strong-style numbers, and cross-reference formatting are evidence only.

coverage_contract.routing_principle: Prefer complete scenes, intercalations, controversy exchanges, parable clusters, discourse movements, miracle cycles, trial sequences, passion episodes, tomb report, and the received ending coordinate; preserve exact competing routes.

second_temple_primary.classification: direct-period context eligible only with source-specific dating and provenance
second_temple_primary.guard: No external Second Temple primary source was read; any future use may inform context but cannot dictate a boundary, identity, fulfillment, theology, or history.

modern_second_temple_reconstruction.guard: Must expose evidence chain and uncertainty and remain non-authoritative for seams.

early_rabbinic_reception.classification: reception/comparative evidence requiring source-specific dating, redaction, and transmission controls

later_rabbinic_reception.classification: reception only, never direct first-century context

routing_principle: Use visible participant, setting, time, action, speech, question-answer, intercalation, parable, refrain, and closure evidence. Rapid kai/euthys chaining alone neither forces a split nor a merge. All decisions remain LOW and deferred.

hardest_seams.risk: Opening label, composite quotation, variant pressure, baptism, testing, and proclamation onset can be over-merged or atomized.
Rapid immediately chaining can hide real synagogue, house, evening, and withdrawal movements.
Question-answer continuity competes with participant and setting resets.
Breaking the family-scribes-family frame can suppress the parent; merging can suppress the inner controversy.

hardest_seams.exact_alternative: one Mark.4.1-Mark.4.34 discourse parent or individual parable units
hardest_seams.risk: Audience shift, explanation, repeated hearing sayings, and parable catalogue allow several defensible levels.
Sea crossings and linked encounters create a macro while each request-action-response scene remains complete.
Mission sending/return can frame the Herod report, while 6.30 begins the feeding movement.
Feeding, sea movement, and landing healings are linked but reset location and action.
Later purity categories, Synoptic parallels, and geography must not dictate seams.
Confession, prediction, following sayings, mountain scene, and descent explanation interlock across a chapter edge.
Prediction, greatness, reception, outsider, stumbling, and salt sayings can be proof-texted or over-split.
Marriage, children, wealth, prediction, rank, and service must not become policy or doctrine chunks.
The fig-tree sandwich must remain visible; received-coordinate 11.26 selects no reading.

hardest_seams.current_route: seven controversy, teaching, and observation units
hardest_seams.risk: Question cycles link rhetorically but retain distinct challengers and forms; widow scene may contrast with prior warning.
Canonical imagery and Synoptic parallels must not create a timetable or import seams.
Plot frame and anointing scene are both independently addressable; no burial or atonement conclusion.
Temporal continuity competes with strong setting and action resets; no harmonized passion chronology.
Intercut locations and repeated prediction relation support both parent and separate scenes.

hardest_seams.current_route: Roman hearing + mockery + crucifixion + death + burial
hardest_seams.risk: Time and actor resets matter; canonical echoes cannot authorize atonement, identity, collective guilt, or history.

hardest_seams.current_route: one tomb report and flight scene
hardest_seams.exact_alternative: Mark.15.42-Mark.16.8 burial-to-tomb parent or Mark.16.1-Mark.16.5 + Mark.16.6-Mark.16.8
hardest_seams.risk: Fearful close and relation to 14.28 cannot decide historicity, resurrection doctrine, or the next textual seam.
Received coordinates and canonical parallels cannot authenticate, reject, rank, or canonically adjudicate any witness or reading.
